For example, $8$ has exactly three double-base representations: $(8)$, $(2,6)$ and $(1,3,4)$, of lengths $1,2,3$. For $n=0$ the only double-base representation is the empty one, $()$ (length $0$).

A **strictly-chained** double-base representation of $n$ is a double-base representation $(n_1,\dots,n_r)$ in which $n_k$ divides $n_{k+1}$ for all $1\le k<r$. For example, $8$ has exactly two strictly-chained double-base representations, $(8)$ and $(2,6)$ (but $(1,3,4)$ is not one). The number $0$ has only the empty strictly-chained representation $()$.

Find the number of strictly-chained double-base representations of $2025$. (You may use $p(0)=p(1)=1$ together with the recurrences: $p(m)=p(m-1)+p(m/3)$ for $3\mid m$; $p(m)=p(\lfloor m/2\rfloor)$ for $m\equiv2\pmod3$; and $p(3m+1)=p(m)+p(3\lfloor\frac{m+1}2\rfloor-1)$ for $m\ge1$.)
